intro: If you're living in one of Newtongrange's older stone-built terraces and the thought of stepping over a bath has started to feel like a genuine hazard, a wet room might be exactly what your home needs. Wet rooms have become one of the most popular bathroom upgrades across Midlothian — and in Newtongrange particularly, they offer a practical solution for households looking to modernise without completely gutting a character property. Whether you're planning ahead for accessibility, want a cleaner and more contemporary look, or simply need to make better use of a compact bathroom space, a properly installed wet room transforms daily life. This guide covers what's involved, what it costs locally, and what to watch out for.
localContext: Newtongrange presents a genuinely varied picture when it comes to wet room installations. The town's older stone-built properties and period cottages — many of which date back to the mining era — often have solid stone floors, narrow bathroom layouts, and original pipework that needs careful assessment before any waterproofing work begins. These properties can be more complex to work with, but they're also robust, and a skilled installer will know how to work with the existing structure rather than against it. On the newer modern estates, the work tends to be more straightforward, with accessible joists and standard plumbing configurations. One factor worth noting across Newtongrange is the moderately hard water supply. While it's far from the worst in Scotland, limescale can gradually affect shower heads, screens, and pump units over time — so it's worth specifying fittings and grout that are easier to maintain in harder water conditions. A good local installer will factor this into their material recommendations.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation in Newtongrange typically follows a clear sequence of work, though the specifics depend heavily on your existing bathroom setup. The process begins with a thorough survey of the space — checking floor structure, drainage position, existing water supply, and whether the subfloor can support a tanked system. In older properties especially, this stage sometimes uncovers issues like corroded pipework or uneven floors that need addressing first. Once the preparatory work is done, the room is stripped back, and the waterproofing system — usually a tanked liner or liquid membrane applied to walls and floor — is installed. This is the most critical part of the job, and it needs time to cure properly before tiling begins. The floor is graded to fall towards the drain, which in older Newtongrange homes may mean building up the floor level slightly to achieve the correct angle. Tiling then follows, along with fitting the drain, shower valve, screen or partition if required, and any additional fixtures like heated towel rails or recessed niching. A full wet room installation typically takes between five and ten working days depending on complexity. You should expect a period of limited bathroom access, so planning around this is important — particularly if it's your only bathroom, which is common in many Newtongrange properties.
pricing: In Newtongrange, a wet room installation typically costs between £6,500 and £11,500 for a full conversion, including labour, waterproofing, tiling, drain, and shower fitting. At the lower end, you're looking at a modern estate property with straightforward access and minimal prep work needed. Costs rise significantly for older stone-built properties where floors need building up, pipework requires updating, or the layout needs reconfiguring. The choice of tiles, shower valve, and fittings also makes a meaningful difference — quality materials suited to Newtongrange's moderately hard water conditions are worth the extra investment. Always get a detailed written quote that separates labour from materials, and factor in any remedial work flagged during the initial survey.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who regularly works in Newtongrange and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely matters for a job like this. They'll be familiar with the construction quirks of the older stone-built housing stock, know the typical drainage configurations found locally, and won't be surprised by the things that occasionally come up in period properties — because they've seen them before. Local tradespeople also tend to have established relationships with suppliers in the region, which can help keep material costs sensible and lead times shorter. And if anything needs attention after the job is complete, they're nearby — not a call centre routing you through a national contractor.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built property in Newtongrange?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — though it requires more preparation than a newer build. Stone floors and older pipework need careful assessment first. In many Newtongrange period properties, the floor level needs building up slightly to create the correct drainage gradient. An experienced installer will survey the space thoroughly before quoting, so there are no surprises mid-job.

faqs.q: How long will the installation take and will I be without a bathroom?
faqs.a: Most wet room installations in Newtongrange take between five and ten working days, depending on the property and specification. You'll have limited or no bathroom access for much of that time. If it's your only bathroom, discuss this with your installer upfront — some homeowners arrange temporary alternatives, and a good tradesperson will sequence the work to minimise disruption where possible.

faqs.q: Does the moderately hard water in Newtongrange cause problems in wet rooms?
faqs.a: It can contribute to limescale build-up on shower heads, screens, and around drains over time. It's not severe in Newtongrange, but it's worth specifying easy-clean grout, a quality thermostatic valve, and a shower head with anti-limescale nozzles. Regular maintenance — descaling every few months — will keep things looking good and functioning well for years.

faqs.q: What's the difference in cost between a basic and a high-spec wet room in Newtongrange?
faqs.a: A straightforward installation in a modern estate property with mid-range tiles and fittings might come in around £6,500–£7,500. A premium spec — bespoke large-format tiles, designer drain, digital shower controls, and underfloor heating — in an older property with more preparatory work could reach £11,000–£12,000. The waterproofing and drainage quality should never be compromised regardless of budget.
